context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present transactions for a mid-size payment processor and provides case management for fraud analysts. Its core purpose is to screen authorizations, block fraudulent transactions, and maintain immutable audit logs while complying with PCI-DSS Level 1.]

## Key Elements
- [Payment Processor / Merchant Systems]
- [Fraud Analyst]
- [Risk Operations Manager / Data Scientist]
- [Payment Gateway / Processor Core]
- [Identity Provider (IdP)]
- [API Gateway / Ingress (AWS API Gateway / ALB)]
- [Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)]
- [Case Management Backend (AWS Lambda / DynamoDB)]
- [Audit & Compliance Store (Amazon S3 Object Lock / Amazon QLDB)]
- [Rule & Model Registry (S3 / DynamoDB)]

## Relationships
- [Customer Systems to API Gateway via REST / gRPC]
- [Fraud Analyst to Case Management via HTTPS / OIDC]
- [Payment Gateway to Scoring Engine via gRPC / mTLS]
- [Scoring Engine to Audit Store via AWS SDK / KMS]
- [Case Management to DynamoDB via AWS PrivateLink]

## Technology Stack
- [AWS Cloud Infrastructure: Chosen for managed services within the 25k EUR monthly budget and EU-West-1 regional residency]
- [AWS ECS Fargate: Selected for Scoring Engine to eliminate Lambda cold starts and guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency]
- [Amazon DynamoDB: Used for case management and rule metadata due to sub-millisecond retrieval performance]
- [Amazon S3 Object Lock & Amazon QLDB: Deployed for tamper-evident, 7-year audit logging to meet compliance mandates]
- [AWS KMS: Used for data-at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys for card data protection]

## Rationale
[This architecture satisfies strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability requirements while maintaining a sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Furthermore, the serverless and managed container design fits the operational constraints of a three-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-time Payment Fraud Screening Platform: Screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time, and provides case management for fraud analysts reviewing suspicious payments.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Scoring API (Go)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js)
- Case Management UI (React)
- Audit & Event Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL)
- Payment Gateway / Processor Core
- Identity Provider (IdP)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Processor Core -> Fraud Scoring API (gRPC / mTLS)
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management UI (HTTPS / OIDC)
- Fraud Scoring API -> Audit & Event Store (TCP/TLS)
- Case Management Backend -> Audit & Event Store (TCP/TLS)
- Case Management UI -> Case Management Backend (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Go: Embedded ONNX runtime for sub-millisecond fraud scoring latency
- Node.js & React: Streamlined case management workflows for fraud analysts
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Tamper-evident, 7-year append-only audit data retention
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget
- AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: PCI-DSS Level 1 encryption and secret management

## Rationale
[Embedding ONNX directly into the Go-based Fraud Scoring API eliminates network hops to meet the strict 50ms P99 latency requirement while reducing operational overhead for a three-engineer team. Furthermore, utilizing AWS managed services ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and immutable 7-year auditability within the fixed budget.]

Fraud Scoring API.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to protect merchant revenue while ensuring strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It provides sub-50ms fraud scoring alongside case management and 7-year tamper-evident audit logging.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Processor Core
- Fraud Scoring API (Go, Embedded ONNX Runtime)
- API Router & Validator (Go)
- Feature Assembler (Go)
- Inference Engine (Go, Embedded ONNX Runtime)
- Audit Dispatcher (Go)
- Amazon SQS FIFO Queue
- Amazon S3 Object Lock
- Case Management Backend (Node.js) & Case Management UI (React)
- Audit & Event Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL)
- AWS ECS on AWS Fargate & AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Processor Core -> Fraud Scoring API: Routes authorization requests [gRPC / mTLS]
- API Router & Validator -> Feature Assembler: Passes sanitized request and correlation ID [Go method call]
- Feature Assembler -> Inference Engine: Passes assembled feature vector [Go method call]
- Inference Engine -> Audit Dispatcher: Emits scoring result, explanation, and model version [Go channel / async]
- Audit Dispatcher -> Amazon SQS FIFO: Offloads signed audit payloads [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Amazon SQS FIFO -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Batches immutable audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Fraud Scoring Audit -> Audit & Event Store: Persists structured relational case data [TCP/TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency performance and minimal memory footprint.
- Embedded ONNX Runtime: Executes machine learning models locally in-process to maintain P99 decision latency below 50 ms.
- AWS ECS on AWS Fargate: Provides container orchestration within the 25k EUR budget without managing underlying servers.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Delivers cost-effective, cryptographically secure WORM storage satisfying 7-year auditability.
- AWS KMS: Handles envelope encryption for audit payloads and model integrity.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples the high-throughput, low-latency scoring hot path from analytical storage using asynchronous queues and in-process execution, ensuring the system meets strict performance and budget constraints. Cryptographic signing and S3 Object Lock guarantee uncompromised 7-year auditability and PCI-DSS compliance.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present transactions, provides case management for fraud analysts, and maintains tamper-evident audit logs. Its core purpose is to screen payment authorizations for fraud within strict latency limits while complying with PCI-DSS Level 1.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst [person]
- Risk Operations Manager / Data Scientist [person]
- Case Management Backend [container] (Node.js monolith on AWS Fargate)
- API Router / Controller [component]
- Case Service [component]
- Case Analytics & Metrics Service [component]
- Audit Logger Component [component]
- Audit & Event Store [container] (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL with read-replicas)
- Identity Provider (IdP) [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Case Management UI -> API Router / Controller: Sends API requests for case workflows [HTTPS]
- API Router / Controller -> Identity Provider (IdP): Validates JWTs [HTTPS]
- API Router / Controller -> Case Service: Routes case workflows [Internal]
- API Router / Controller -> Case Analytics & Metrics Service: Requests KPI reports [Internal]
- Case Service -> Audit & Event Store: Persists case updates and audit trails [TCP/TLS]
- Case Analytics & Metrics Service -> Audit & Event Store: Queries historical case data [TCP/TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js with Express: Powers the Case Management Backend monolith for rapid development by a 3-person team.
- AWS Fargate (ECS): Hosts the containerized backend without control-plane management overhead to fit within budget.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Provides scalable relational storage with dedicated read-replicas for analytics.
- AWS Secrets Manager & KMS: Manages secrets and secures tamper-evident audit logs via cryptographic signing.
- Terraform: Automates infrastructure provisioning and ensures secure, repeatable deployments.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a monolithic Node.js container on AWS Fargate to minimize operational complexity for a three-person team within a 25,000 EUR/month budget. Dedicated Aurora PostgreSQL read-replicas and cryptographic signing satisfy strict PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year audit requirements without compromising real-time performance.

Case Management UI.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management UI is a React Single Page Application hosted on AWS S3 and CloudFront that provides fraud analysts with tools to review suspicious payment transactions. It delivers secure queue prioritization, masked card data rendering, and decision explainability visualization while complying with PCI-DSS Level 1.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Case Management UI (React Container)
  - Authentication Wrapper Component
  - Dashboard & Queue View Component
  - Case Detail & Explainability View Component
  - Action & Audit Logger Component
- Case Management Backend (Node.js Container)
- Identity Provider (IdP) (External System)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Authentication Wrapper: Authenticates session [HTTPS / OIDC]
- Authentication Wrapper -> Identity Provider (IdP): Manages OIDC session [HTTPS / OIDC]
- Dashboard & Queue View -> Case Management Backend: Fetches prioritized queues and SLA metrics [HTTPS / REST]
- Case Detail & Explainability View -> Case Management Backend: Retrieves transaction details and model feature attributions [HTTPS / REST]
- Action & Audit Logger -> Case Management Backend: Submits analyst decisions and audit payloads [HTTPS / REST]

## Technology Stack
- React SPA: Chosen for rapid analyst workflows and streamlined component architecture.
- AWS S3 & CloudFront: Selected for zero operational overhead, global caching, and strict CSP header enforcement.
- HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict Cookies: Mandated for secure OIDC token storage against XSS.

## Rationale
This architecture fits the requirements by maintaining strict PCI-DSS scope separation and auditability within a 3-engineer team capacity. Leveraging managed AWS services and stateless frontend components keeps infrastructure costs well below the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Audit & Event Store.analysis:
## Overview
The Audit & Event Store is a secure, cost-effective component of the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening Platform designed to maintain tamper-evident audit logs and transaction data for 7 years. It ensures compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 while adhering to strict infrastructure budget and small-team constraints.

## Key Elements
- Event Ingestion Service (Go, AWS ECS Fargate): Receives audit events via gRPC/mTLS and validates schemas.
- Relational Ledger Store (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL): Stores hot audit data with `pg_audit` enabled for 90 days.
- Archival Worker (AWS Lambda, Python): Periodically archives historical data to long-term storage.
- S3 Glacier Object Lock Bucket (AWS S3): Provides WORM (Write-Once-Read-Many) storage for 7-year regulatory retention.
- Network Load Balancer (AWS NLB): Routes high-throughput internal traffic to ingestion tasks.
- AWS Secrets Manager / IAM: Manages dynamic credentials and database authentication.

## Relationships
- Fraud Scoring API -> Event Ingestion Service [gRPC/mTLS]
- Case Management Backend -> Event Ingestion Service [gRPC/mTLS]
- Event Ingestion Service -> Relational Ledger Store [SQL/TLS]
- Archival Worker -> Relational Ledger Store [SQL/TLS]
- Archival Worker -> S3 Glacier Object Lock [HTTPS/TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency event ingestion processing.
- Python: Utilized for lightweight serverless archival batch tasks.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Provides scalable relational storage with native audit logging (`pg_audit`).
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Enforces tamper-evident, cost-effective long-term data compliance.
- AWS ECS Fargate & NLB: Enables auto-scaling container execution without managing underlying servers.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services like S3 Object Lock and Aurora PostgreSQL to minimize maintenance overhead for a three-engineer team. Tiered storage controls costs to stay within the €25,000 monthly budget while meeting stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability mandates.
